status_summary: The America First Trade Policy memorandum of 2025-01-20 assigned trade reviews to USTR, Commerce, Treasury and OMB rather than naming USTR the single lead. USTR's FY2027 budget justification (cover dated March 2026) requests 95 million dollars and 301 FTE for Salaries and Expenses, against 65 million dollars and 230 FTE enacted for that account in FY2026; counting the Trade Enforcement Trust Fund, the document describes the increase as 7 million dollars and 27 FTE. On advisory committees, USTR published notices on 2026-03-04 and 2026-03-12 continuing the main committees for new four-year terms, with ability to advance the America First Trade Policy listed as a selection factor, and a renewed charter for one industry committee was filed on 2026-07-16, so the legacy committees were continued with changed criteria rather than disposed of.

timeline.event: The President signed the America First Trade Policy memorandum, assigning separate trade reviews to USTR, Commerce and Treasury, with reports due by 2025-04-01 (published 2025-01-30).
USTR published a notice continuing the Advisory Committee for Trade Policy and Negotiations and seeking nominations, listing ability to advance America First Trade Policy among selection factors.
USTR and Commerce published a notice continuing the Industry Trade Advisory Committees (15 committees plus a chairs committee) and seeking applications.
USTR's FY2027 budget justification (cover dated March 2026) requested 95 million dollars and 301 FTE for Salaries and Expenses, up from 65 million dollars and 230 FTE enacted for FY2026.

The renewed charter of the Industry Trade Advisory Committee on Energy and Energy Services (ITAC 7), established jointly by Commerce and USTR under the Trade Act of 1974, was filed, renewing the committee rather than terminating it; the USTR signature line shows two July 2026 dates.

title: Empower USTR to lead trade policy and dispose of legacy advisory committees
uncertainties: The budget justification's cover gives only March 2026, so the day in its date is approximate. Only one renewed industry committee charter (ITAC 7) was opened; other renewed charters were seen in search results but not read. The ITAC 7 charter text does not state a term length, so the 2026 to 2030 term rests on the March 2026 notice and the charter's file name, and its USTR signature line shows two different July 2026 days. Whether USTR or White House economic staff led tariff decisions in practice was not resolved; the January 2025 memorandum splits reviews among several offices. FY2027 appropriations status was not checked. A Federal Register search of USTR documents from 2026-03-13 to 2026-10-23 found no notice terminating or restructuring advisory committees. The budget justification is kept as a dated formal submission to Congress rather than an operative action. The progress figure is an inference. Leadership of trade agreements is also covered by c26-05.
